hook.speaker: Bhasa
hook.setting: Two childhood friends meet again in old age; one admits he never found peace.
hook.sanskrit: उह्यमानमनन्तेषु चेतः कार्यमहोर्मिषु । क्षणमेति न विश्रान्तिं चिन्ताताण्डविताशयम् ॥ इदं कृतं करोमीदं करिष्यामीदमित्यलम् । कलनाजालवलिता मूर्च्छिता मतिपक्षिणी ॥
hook.line: 'Done this, doing this, must do that.' Caught in endless lists, the mind never gets a moment's rest.
hook.translation: Carried along on endless great waves of tasks, the mind never gets a moment's rest; its depths dance with worry. 'This I've done, this I'm doing, this I'll do': so the bird of the mind, tangled in a net of reckonings, faints.
hook.why: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.

prasang.title: Two old friends meet again and admit they never found peace
prasang.summary: Bhasa and Vilasa grow up inseparable in a forest hermitage. After their fathers die they drift apart and spend long lonely years in hard austerities. When they meet again as old men, one asks if the other is well; he answers honestly that there is no wellness while the mind keeps spinning through endless tasks and worries.
prasang.story_hook: They had been inseparable as boys, and when they met again they were old men with nothing to show.
prasang.lesson: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.

hook.for_you: Your mind won't settle while you are working, and a verse was chosen with that weight in mind.

alternates.speaker: Arjuna
alternates.setting: Arjuna, seeing his own family in the enemy ranks, collapses in grief before the battle.
alternates.sanskrit: सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति । वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते ॥ गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिदह्यते । न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः ॥
alternates.line: Shaking limbs, a dry mouth, a racing body: the Gita opens with a panic attack, not a hero.
alternates.translation: My limbs give way, my mouth is parched, my body trembles and my hair stands on end.
alternates.why: Even the strongest people freeze; the Gita begins with a breakdown, not a hero.
alternates.misuse: Not a dismissal of anxiety; it shows that even the strong feel it, and the teaching starts there.

prasang.title: Overcome by delusion, Arjuna speaks in fear, love and grief
prasang.summary: Seeing his kin ready to die, Arjuna trembles, his bow slips, and he argues that no victory is worth killing family. He sits down in the chariot and refuses to fight.
prasang.story_hook: The greatest archer of his age stood between two armies, and his hands began to shake.
prasang.lesson: Even the strongest people freeze; the Gita begins with a breakdown, not a hero.

alternates.speaker: Arjuna
alternates.setting: Arjuna asks what becomes of someone who tries and fails; Krishna reassures him.
alternates.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचअयतिः श्रद्धयोपेतो योगाच्चलितमानसः । अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति ॥
alternates.line: What happens to someone who believes, tries, slips, and doesn't make it to the end?
alternates.translation: Arjuna said: One who has faith but does not strive enough, whose mind falls away from yoga before reaching perfection, what end does he come to, Krishna?
alternates.why: No sincere effort is wasted; you pick up where you left off.

prasang.title: What becomes of one who falls from yoga
prasang.summary: Arjuna fears that one who falls short is lost like a torn cloud. Krishna promises that no one who does good comes to ruin; past effort carries forward and they strive again.
prasang.lesson: No sincere effort is wasted; you pick up where you left off.

verse.speaker: Janaka
verse.setting: Janaka, having chosen to keep ruling, talks gently to his own restless mind at night.
verse.sanskrit: यथा यथा विकल्पौघान्संकल्पयसि हेलया । तथा तथैति स्फारत्वं संसारस्तव चिन्तया ॥
verse.line: The more scenarios you spin, the bigger your world of worry grows.
verse.translation: The more you casually spin up fancies and possibilities, the more your world of troubles swells, through your own worrying.
verse.why: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

prasang.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
prasang.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
prasang.story_hook: One spring morning, a king out for a walk overheard a song that he could not stop thinking about.
prasang.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

verse.for_you: You are rehearsing a conversation that has not happened yet. The spinning is keeping your world small. Let the calendar stay blank for a little while.
verse.try_today: Notice one thought you are spinning and let it drop without rehearsal.

why: Worry grows when you feed it (Yoga Vasishtha 5.21.6)
the swelling is traced to the spinning, which can be stopped

verse.line: No winter was but summer came behind,
verse.translation: No winter was but summer came behind, Each hollow crests the wave, They push each other in light and shade; Be steady then and brave.
verse.why: No struggle is wasted; hold on a little longer.

prasang.title: 'Hold on yet a while, brave heart' (poem to the Maharaja of Khetri)
prasang.summary: A short poem of encouragement to a friend. Clouds hide the sun for a while, summer always follows winter, and no honest struggle is wasted even when hopes fail.
prasang.lesson: No struggle is wasted; hold on a little longer.

verse.for_you: The waiting for your promotion results is a heavy winter that feels endless right now, but the text reminds us that no winter stays. Light and shade only push each other along. Let yourself be steady in this waiting.
verse.try_today: Notice one small shift between light and shade in your day and let it be enough.

verse.speaker: Bhushunda
verse.setting: Bhushunda, the ancient crow, tells Vasishtha why he lives long and well.
verse.sanskrit: किमद्य मम संपन्नं प्रातर्वा भविता पुनः । इति चिन्ताज्वरो नास्ति तेन जीवाम्यनामयः ॥
verse.line: 'What happened today? What comes tomorrow?' I don't run that fever. That's why I live well.
verse.translation: 'What has happened to me today? What will come tomorrow?' I have no such fever of worry; so I live long, free of illness.
verse.why: A long, steady life comes from a mind that stays in the present, wants little and stays kind.

prasang.title: Bhushunda, the crow who outlived the ages
prasang.summary: Vasishtha travels to a wish-fulfilling tree on Mount Meru to meet Bhushunda, a crow who has watched world-ages come and go. Asked how he has lived so long, untroubled, Bhushunda lists his habits: he doesn't brood on the past or future, doesn't fret about what he'll get next, doesn't grow arrogant from knowing, and shares in others' joys and sorrows.
prasang.story_hook: High on a mountain lived a crow who had watched whole ages of the world rise and fall.
prasang.lesson: A long, steady life comes from a mind that stays in the present, wants little and stays kind.

verse.for_you: You are caught in a fever of what might come, rehearsing a future that is not here. The promotion is not decided, and the conversation has not happened. You can set down the worry and let today be a place to rest.
verse.try_today: Notice when your mind rehearses the future, and return your attention to the chair beneath you.
verse.scene_line: You check the calendar and rehearse the conversation while Bhushunda simply watches the world-ages pass.

why: Do not chase the future or brood on the past.
worry is called a fever he does not run

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu on how a free person moves through the world.
verse.sanskrit: प्राप्तकर्मकरो नित्यं शत्रुमित्रसमानदृक् । ईहितानीहितैर्मुक्तो न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ॥ सर्वस्याभिमतं वक्ता चोदितः पेशलोक्तिमान् । आशयज्ञश्च भूतानां संसारे नावसीदति ॥
verse.line: Do the work in front of you, speak gently, read people's hearts, and you won't sink in the world.
verse.translation: Always doing the work that comes, seeing friend and foe alike, free of wanting and not-wanting, such a one neither grieves nor craves. Saying what is agreeable to all, speaking gently when asked, knowing the intent of others' hearts, such a one does not sink in the world.
verse.why: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

prasang.title: How a free person lives
prasang.summary: Ribhu describes how a free person lives among others: letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes, doing the work at hand, speaking gently, busy outside and calm inside, and treating the whole world as family.
prasang.lesson: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

verse.for_you: You are rehearsing a conversation that is not yet here. The work in front of you is what is happening right now. Let the promotion results come when they come; they do not need your worry to arrive.
verse.try_today: Do the one task that is right in front of you, and let the rest be.
verse.scene_line: You watch your manager's calendar instead of the work that is waiting for you.

verse.speaker: Ram
verse.setting: King Ram calls the whole city together and tells them how to treat what he says.
verse.sanskrit: सोइ सेवक प्रियतम मम सोई। मम अनुसासन मानै जोई॥ जौं अनीति कछु भाषौं भाई। तौ मोहि बरजहु भय बिसराई ॥
verse.line: If I say anything wrong, stop me. Don't be afraid.
verse.translation: "The one who follows my teaching is truly my dear servant. But if I say anything unjust, brothers, put aside your fear and stop me."
verse.why: A good leader invites correction; a good life is simple, honest and free of grudges.

prasang.title: Ram's address to the citizens
prasang.summary: Ram calls his people together and says he speaks without pride of rank: if he says anything wrong, stop him without fear. The way he recommends needs no grand effort, only a simple nature, an honest mind, contentment, and no grudges, no quarrels, no craving and no fear.
prasang.lesson: A good leader invites correction; a good life is simple, honest and free of grudges.

verse.for_you: Your mind is rehearsing every possible outcome until the results arrive. You are allowed to let the outcome be unknown. Rest in the fact that your worth is not decided by a promotion.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment today when you choose not to rehearse the outcome.
verse.scene_line: You stand before your manager, and Ram stands before the people of Ayodhya.
